processing: Green tea of one bud with one leaf, or one bud with two just-opening leaves, fixed and then baked dry.
harvest_season: Picking opens about ten days before Qingming.
appearance_dry: Orchid-like shape with slightly rounded strips, jade green and visibly downy.
appearance_wet: Tender shoots at this plucking standard, as is usual for an early spring green.
taste_profile: Fresh, brisk and sweetly mellow, with a lasting orchid aroma.

brewing.notes: General settings for a very early green. Cooler water protects the orchid note.

vintage_note: An early-spring tea, opening about ten days before Qingming, and usually drunk from the current year's harvest as with other Shaanxi greens. The earliest lots are the ones to seek.
description:
Long'an Bixuan is a modern green tea from Langao County in Ankang, southern Shaanxi, in the Qinba mountains. It grows at the foot of a national forest park and is part of the local Long'an tea line.

The leaf is picked very early, about ten days before Qingming, then fixed and baked.

In the cup it is fresh and sweetly mellow, with a clear liquor and a lasting orchid aroma. Keep the water moderate, because early leaf scorches easily.

It is mostly a regional tea, so finding it means asking for Langao origin specifically. Selenium and zinc are often promoted with Ankang teas; buy it for the cup.
history: The tea is young and its origin is unusually clear. The Shaanxi science and technology commission took it up in 1987 as part of a Qinba mountains forestry-products development project, and it was completed, appraised at provincial level and given its name in 1990.
